correctness.rationale: For all integers b>=2 and m>=3, the exact increment law 1-(b-1)nu_b(n+1) modulo m implies each adjacent pair of increments contains +1. Reversal of a legal triple forces its increments to be (+1,-1) or (-1,+1), hence every reversible triple is palindromic. The two overlapping triples of a hypothetical reversible length-four word force an alternating word, whose reverse would need forbidden (-1,+1,-1) increments. Multiples of b cannot occur two apart for b>=3; for b=2 one of the two even integers two apart has valuation exactly one and increment zero. The prohibition propagates to every length>=4. Translation invariance and digit-carry construction give exactly m^2/g two-letter factors and the gcd-specific reversal orbit counts. All lemmas are fully proved in RESULT.md. A standalone independent implementation checked 1406 symbolic (b,m) pairs, 24843 exact arithmetic witnesses and 20 direct 100000-symbol prefix languages. The finite checks supplement rather than establish the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The 2024 motivating publication states the base-two, modulus-three special case, which is explicitly excluded from the novelty claim. The uniform result for all bases and all moduli at least three, its exact gcd-dependent length-two orbit counts, and its sharp length-two/length-four reversal-free transition are not equivalent to any checked primary statement. Existing dihedral antimorphisms alter symbols and do not imply ordinary reversal. No dominating all-parameter result was found in the inspected full source texts or published-result searches. Search absence is not a mathematical proof of priority.
residual_risks: An unindexed or inaccessible source may already state a universal ordinary-reversal avoidance result for all generalized Thue–Morse words.
The 2011 dihedral symmetry theorem can be related to ordinary reversal through extra arguments, though its stated conclusion is not this one.

value.rationale: The reversal quotient is a named combinatorics-on-words complexity invariant with an explicit 2024 generalized Thue–Morse motivation. The theorem gives a complete infinite two-parameter classification of reversal collisions, a sharp gcd phase transition in the minimal reversal-free length, and exact length-two quotient counts. It allows any established factor complexity formula to be transferred directly to reflection complexity at lengths at least three; it is neither a finite isolated table nor a restatement of a known binary specialization.
